disclosures.name: TestGrabConnAllocs
disclosures.reason: Want-zero AllocsPerRun assert on Conn.grabConn: Go allocates nothing. The converted path allocates 96 bytes per run (96,000 bytes over 1,000 runs on windows and linux, at go1.24.13 and go1.26.10) and golib's counter charges none of it, so the 96 the test prints (`Conn.grabConn allocated 96 objects; want 0`) is a byte figure and no object count exists to compare with the want. What remains is outside the counter.

disclosures.name: TestRawBytesAllocs
disclosures.reason: Want-zero AllocsPerRun assert (the test fails above 0.5) over fourteen convertAssign cases into a pre-sized RawBytes: Go's escape analysis keeps the temporaries off the heap. The converted run counts 28 objects per run at go1.24.13, two per call over the fourteen cases, and 11 per run at go1.26.10 on windows and linux (identical test body). Boxing into `any` is not counted; which objects are counted is not yet attributed. Candidate sites are strconv formatBits' local array (strconv/itoa.cs:89), which six of the cases reach through asBytes, and the reflect path's Value construction on every call.
